synopsis: Across 100-plus site types, 10-plus scenarios, weather/light conditions and machine variants, the booklet estimates more than 7,000 validation strata; adding finer parameters produces millions of combinations, making exhaustive field coverage infeasible [f131, f11331, f132]. It recommends structuring testing through an operating-domain taxonomy, a scenario catalog and parameterized scenario families, with site dimensions represented as attributes and impossible combinations explicitly excluded [f119, f6727, f6762]. Scenario counts alone do not establish coverage: nearly identical sites can contribute little diversity, expert catalogs miss unanticipated scenarios, and no source quantifies how environmental diversity relates to failures found [f4064, f6775, f4379]. A four-month simulation window forces tiered fidelity, while simulation can cover the otherwise infeasible interior only after physical boundary testing and independent validation establish predictive credibility [f13548, f8061]. Combinatorial testing can shrink test suites but does not establish that low-order interactions suffice for collision avoidance; the booklet also recommends separating coverage, failure discovery and statistical estimation streams [f4332, f11334].
